claim.pdf_says: [ LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 / literal-4 } ]  ...   (a TALL outer bracket opens before LOCALE and closes after the brace pair; the ellipsis is outside it)
claim.markdown_says: `LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 / literal-4 }` ...   (ISO_COBOL.md line 13928 - no outer bracket)
claim.why_it_matters: Same class of loss as the CURRENCY line: the bracket that makes the LOCALE clause optional inside SPECIAL-NAMES is gone, so the transcription reads as though every SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph must carry a LOCALE clause, and the '...' now binds to the brace pair instead of to the whole clause.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by independent render at 300 dpi and again at 600 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v320/spec_p320.png, E:/Temp/specrecon/v320_600/spec_p320.png; crops locale_left.png / locale_right.png). PRINTED GLYPHS, read directly: immediately left of the word LOCALE stands a TALL SQUARE BRACKET '[' - a single vertical rule whose top and bottom serifs both turn RIGHT - spanning the full two-line height of the external-locale-name-1 / literal-4 stack. At the right end, reading left to right, the tall closing BRACE '}' is followed by a SEPARATE tall SQUARE BRACKET ']' - a vertical rule whose top and bottom serifs both turn LEFT - and only then, OUTSIDE that bracket, the ellipsis. Neither delimiter carries choice-indicator bars (single stroke, no doubled vertical). So the PDF prints exactly: [ LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 | literal-4 } ] ... . The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13928 reads verbatim: `LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 / literal-4 }` ... - the outer bracket pair is absent, and it is absent from the source text, not merely from a rendered view (verified with `cat -A`, no stray characters, no reflow onto an adjacent line; the whole clause is one line with blank lines either side). REFUTATION ATTEMPTS, ALL FAILED: (1) the bracket is not reflowed to an adjacent line - lines 13927 and 13929 are '[ dynamic-length-structure-clause ] ...' and a blank line; (2) it is not a transcription convention that drops outer brackets, because the immediately surrounding lines of the SAME figure keep theirs verbatim ('[ CRT STATUS IS data-name-2 ]', '[ DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA ]', '[ dynamic-length-structure-clause ] ...', '[ symbolic-characters-clause ] ...', '[ ORDER TABLE ordering-name-1 IS literal-9 ] .'); (3) the backtick code span is not a bracket surrogate - it carries no delimiter semantics and the CLASS and switch-name figures on the same page transcribe their outer brackets as real drawn glyphs; (4) it is not page-break furniture, hyphenation, or wrapping. MEANING CHANGE IS REAL AND NORMATIVE, on both counts the claim states. Optionality: '[ X ] ...' is zero-or-more; bare 'X ...' is one-or-more, so the transcription makes a LOCALE clause MANDATORY in every SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph. This contradicts the spec's own prose - 12.3.7.4 GR (ISO_COBOL.md:14234) says 'When the LOCALE clause is specified, locale-name-1 references a locale...', i.e. it may be omitted - and contradicts the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph being optional at all. Ellipsis binding: ISO's own convention (ISO_COBOL.md:2705) is mechanical - 'scanning right to left, determine the right bracket or right brace delimiter immediately to the left of the ellipsis; continue scanning right to left and determine the logically matching left ... delimiter; the ellipsis applies to the portion of the format between the determined pair'. In the PDF the nearest right delimiter is ']', matching the '[' before LOCALE, so the ellipsis repeats the WHOLE clause. In the transcription the nearest right delimiter is '}', matching the '{' before external-locale-name-1, so the ellipsis repeats only the operand choice - the transcription licenses 'LOCALE loc-1 IS ext-1 lit-4 ext-2 ...' (one IS, many operands) and forbids a SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph with no LOCALE clause. Both readings are wrong against the printed standard. The claim's PDF quote, markdown quote, line number and rationale are all accurate as written; no correction needed.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as claimed; no correction required. For the record, the exact printed form at page 320 (PDF p.290) 12.3.7.2 is a plain outer bracket with NO choice indicators: [ LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 | literal-4 } ] ... - tall '[' before LOCALE, tall ']' after the closing brace, ellipsis outside the bracket. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13928 drops the outer bracket pair entirely. Fix: restore it, e.g. `[ LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 | literal-4 } ]` ... , and note that the sibling CURRENCY line at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13920 in the same figure carries the identical loss (the PDF prints a tall outer bracket around the whole CURRENCY clause, closing after the inner '[ WITH PICTURE SYMBOL literal-8 ]' and before the ellipsis) - fix both in one change set.
